shape: gen3 contact-flag divergence: gen3 moves.ts both ADDS and REMOVES contact relative to the base data the engine is built from
was: reports/c88 sub-shape C, filed NOT YET DETERMINED

the_boundary.protocol: Rayquaza uses Overheat on Sharpedo; Sharpedo faints; Showdown then emits |-damage|p1a: Rayquaza|189/262|[from] ability: Rough Skin|[of] p2a: Sharpedo
the_boundary.miss: observed_only=[('abilityroughskin', -16)] engine_only=[] -- the engine emits nothing

the_reference.rough_skin: data/mods/gen3/abilities.ts:162-169 overrides roughskin to source.baseMaxhp / 16. Base (modern) is /8. The engine already has the gen3 value.
the_reference.the_actual_cause: data/mods/gen3/moves.ts:470-473 overrides OVERHEAT's flags to { contact: 1, protect: 1, mirror: 1, metronome: 1 }. Base overheat (data/moves.ts) has flags { protect, mirror, metronome } and NO contact. So in gen3 Overheat makes contact and Rough Skin fires.

the_engine.rough_skin: src/gen3/abilities.rs:193 implements ROUGHSKIN correctly -- maxhp/16, attacker's maxhp, gated on damage_dealt > 0 && choice.flags.contact. The ability is not the problem.
the_engine.the_gap: choices.rs builds OVERHEAT from the BASE flag set, with no contact, so choice.flags.contact is false and the ability hook never fires. Note choices.rs:11710 ALREADY forks OVERHEAT on cfg!(feature = "gen3") for base_power (140 vs 130) -- only the flags block was not forked, so there is already a home for the fix.

exhaustive_enumeration.SUPERSEDED_METHOD: 'diff every gen3 moves.ts override carrying contact:1 against the same move in base data/moves.ts'. One-directional by construction, so it could only ever find additions. It also read only data/mods/gen3/moves.ts, while gen3 inherits through gen4, gen5 and up -- a contact flag set in a LATER-gen mod also lands in gen3. finalgambit is exactly that case; it does not exist in gen3, so the additions direction came out right by luck, not by method.
exhaustive_enumeration.corrected_method: resolve the full mod inheritance chain (gen3 -> gen4 -> ... -> base) and compare the EFFECTIVE gen3 flag set against the engine's, in both directions.

exhaustive_enumeration.removals_are_live_bugs_of_the_same_class: the engine fires Rough Skin / Static / Poison Point / Flame Body / Effect Spore / Cute Charm on a gen3 Fake Out, Covet or Feint Attack where Showdown does not. Latent, not observed: zero uses of the three in this 200-game window -- which is exactly why enumeration was supposed to catch them and sampling would not.
exhaustive_enumeration.bide_was_a_grep_artifact: an earlier version listed bide among gen3 overrides carrying contact. It has no flags override in gen3/moves.ts; the contact:1 at gen3/moves.ts:91 is inside bide's nested condition damage move. A tell that the enumeration was textual rather than resolved.

disposition.the_fix: in the gen3 build, ADD contact to OVERHEAT and ANCIENTPOWER, and REMOVE it from COVET, FAKEOUT and FEINTATTACK.
disposition.scope: five moves, two directions, derived by resolving the mod chain rather than grepping one file.
disposition.blast_radius_warning: contact gates six abilities that the gen3 build actually implements, every one of them behind attacker_choice.flags.contact: ROUGHSKIN (abilities.rs:193), POISONPOINT (:672), EFFECTSPORE (:693), CUTECHARM (:721), FLAMEBODY (:745), STATIC (:779). King's Rock is NOT among them -- the gen3 build has no King's Rock at all, so an earlier draft's mention of it was over-inclusion. Changing it in EITHER direction changes behaviour wherever those interact, so this needs the measured treatment C87 got: branch counts, the tactics gate, and a check that no currently-matched row becomes divergent. The three removals have zero observed uses in this window, so the sweep will not evidence them -- they need a targeted probe.

note_on_size: one OBSERVED row in this 200-game window. The three removals are latent. By rows x search-impact this ranks below the matcher shapes; recorded now because the cause is established and the enumeration is finally two-directional.
CORRECTION: an earlier version of this file claimed the shape was 'exactly two moves' and called the enumeration exhaustive. It was not. The method searched gen3 overrides CARRYING contact:1, which structurally cannot find moves where gen3 REMOVES a contact flag the base data has. Review found three such moves. The surface is five, in two directions.
